description: Two-panel composite of thermodynamic (CALPHAD-type) predictions for two medium-Mn lightweight steels, labelled M1 and M2. Both panels share the x-axis "Temperature (°C)", 600–900 with 50 °C ticks, crossed by a vertical dashed line annotated "Intercritical Annealing Temperature (IAT)" at 700 °C (with a downward arrow in (a)). (a): y-axis "Predicted Equilibrium Fraction of Austenite (%)", 0–100 with 10 % ticks; two dash-dot curves, black for M1 and red for M2 (legend upper right), both rising monotonically with temperature; M1 lies above M2 everywhere, approaching the 100 % top tick near 900 °C, while M2 only reaches just under the 60 % gridline at 900 °C. Filled circles mark the IAT: the black point lies between the 40 and 50 % gridlines, labelled "(IAT, austenite % of M1)"; the red point sits just above the 30 % gridline, labelled "(IAT, austenite % of M2)". (b): y-axis "Composition in Austenite (wt.%)", 0–12 with 2 wt.% ticks; curves labelled Mn (highest, two closely spaced curves falling from near the 12 wt.% tick at 600 °C to slightly above the 8 wt.% gridline at 900 °C), Al (rising from just above the 2 wt.% gridline towards midway between 2 and 4 wt.%), Si (falling from just above the 2 wt.% gridline to below it) and C (lowest, staying well below 2 wt.% and declining). Legend: solid = M1, dash-dot = M2. Together the panels justify choosing IAT = 700 °C, where the predicted austenite fraction is moderate and the austenite Mn content is highest.

observations.observation: Panel (a) shows two dash-dot curves of predicted equilibrium austenite fraction that both increase monotonically with temperature between 600 and 900 °C, with the black M1 curve lying above the red M2 curve at every temperature.

In panel (a) the black filled circle on the 700 °C IAT line lies between the 40 and 50 % gridlines and is annotated '(IAT, austenite % of M1)'; the red filled circle lies just above the 30 % gridline and is annotated '(IAT, austenite % of M2)'.
The vertical dashed line in both panels is labelled 'Intercritical Annealing Temperature (IAT)' and is placed at 700 °C on the temperature axis; in (a) it ends in a downward arrow.

Panel (b) is labelled 'Composition in Austenite (wt.%)' with a 0–12 wt.% y-axis (2 wt.% ticks) and separately annotates the element groups Mn, Al, Si and C; Mn is the highest curve group and C the lowest.
The legend of panel (b) gives a solid line for M1 and a dash-dot line for M2, whereas the legend of panel (a) uses black for M1 and red for M2.

The caption states that (a) shows the predicted equilibrium fraction of austenite (γ^eq) at various intercritical annealing (IA) temperatures and (b) the predicted composition of austenite at different temperatures for M1 and M2.

The citing text identifies the two steel compositions as Fe–8Mn–3Al–0.2C (M1) and Fe–8Mn–3Al–1Si-0.2C (M2), fabricated by vacuum arc melting with four remelts, homogenised at 1100 °C for 2 h, hot-rolled at 1100 °C to 50 % thickness reduction, and intercritically annealed for 1 h followed by water quenching.
The citing text states that an IAT of 700 °C was selected corresponding to about 11 wt.% Mn in austenite for both steel compositions.

The citing text asserts that the equilibrium austenite fraction increases with increasing IAT (Fig. 2a) while the austenite-stabilising elements Mn and C decrease in austenite with increasing IAT (Fig. 2b), so austenite stability decreases at higher IAT.
The citing text reports that literature suggests Mn concentrations greater than about 11 wt.% typically give stable austenite, which motivated the 700 °C selection.

The citing text notes that observed austenite fractions in the intercritically annealed samples are lower than the predicted equilibrium austenite fractions of Fig. 2a, attributed to partial transformation of austenite to martensite on cooling.
In panel (b) the Mn curves decrease with temperature from close to the 12 wt.% top tick at 600 °C to slightly above the 8 wt.% gridline at 900 °C, whereas the Al curves increase over the same range.

In panel (a), at 900 °C the M1 curve approaches the 100 % top tick whereas the M2 curve remains just under the 60 % gridline, showing that the Si-containing steel M2 retains a markedly lower predicted austenite fraction at high temperature.

subfigures.description: Line plot of predicted equilibrium austenite fraction (%) versus temperature (600–900 °C). Black dash-dot curve (M1) is above red dash-dot curve (M2) at all temperatures; both increase with temperature. A vertical dashed line marked 'Intercritical Annealing Temperature (IAT)' with a downward arrow sits at 700 °C, carrying a black filled circle (M1, between the 40 and 50 % gridlines, annotated '(IAT, austenite % of M1)') and a red filled circle (M2, just above the 30 % gridline, annotated '(IAT, austenite % of M2)').

Line plot of austenite composition (wt.%) versus temperature (600–900 °C) with a vertical dashed IAT line at 700 °C. Element labels Mn, Al, Si and C annotate curve groups: Mn highest and decreasing from near 12 wt.% to just above the 8 wt.% gridline; Al increasing from just above 2 wt.% towards about midway between the 2 and 4 wt.% gridlines; Si decreasing from just above to below the 2 wt.% gridline; C lowest and decreasing below 2 wt.%. Legend: solid line = M1, dash-dot line = M2.

unreadable_items: panel (b): the legend colour swatches (olive/gold) do not match the curve colours, so which of the two closely spaced Mn curves (red solid vs blue dash-dot) belongs to M1 and which to M2 cannot be resolved with certainty from the pixels
panel (b): the Si panel of the legend region is crowded; assignment of the single green dash-dot Si curve to M1 or M2 is not explicit in the image
